answer: Yes, within limits. The file command (Operational mode) performs basic file and directory operations: rename, view (listing for a file or directory), delete, sha256sum and md5sum. Its parameters are operation, file-path, new-file-path (used only when operation is rename) and result. File system access is restricted to the current user's access, so not all files and directories are editable. Examples: file rename /tmp/a.log /tmp/b.log, file view /tmp, file delete /tmp/a.log, file sha256sum /tmp/a.log. Separately, clear [-f] file filetype target-file removes one particular file; filetype is limited to krp (only one KRP may exist, so target-file is not needed), script (use show script to list them) and swimage (deletes a downloaded swimage that was not yet installed). show file <filename> displays the file contents.

Both are described as performing basic file and directory operations and both run in Operational mode, but file is the fuller command. file-operation takes only operation (rename, delete, view), new-file-path and file-path. file takes operation with five values (rename, delete, view, sha256sum, md5sum), plus file-path, new-file-path (for rename) and a result attribute reporting the file operation result, and it carries the companion forms show file <filename> to display file contents and clear [-f] file <filetype> <target-file> to remove a krp, script or downloaded swimage. So use file for checksums, viewing contents and clearing typed files; file-operation covers only rename/delete/view.

Use add file-server-<name> server-address <value> protocol <value> [server-port] [user-name] [password] [initial-path] [label], available in Operational and Candidate Configuration mode; set, show file-server-<name>, show file-servers and delete file-server-<name> also exist. The protocol values are file, ftp, sftp, scp, http and https. file represents local storage, including USB storage, and requires initial-path to be provided. ftp and http are only applicable when secure-mode is set to false. server-address may be an IPv4 address, IPv6 address or domain name. server-port is optional: if not provided the default for the selected protocol is used. Limits: name 0-64 characters, user-name 0-64, password 0-128, initial-path 0-256, label 0-256.

Use show filetype-<name> [last-completion-status] [last-transfer] [last-duration] [last-operation], available in Operational and Candidate Configuration mode. name is the file type for which the transfer happened. last-transfer is the last transfer start timestamp, a date-time in the format YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ssZ (see the set-time command). last-duration is the last transfer duration as a time-interval, last-completion-status is the last transfer status, and last-operation is the last transfer operation with values unknown, upload or download. Note that transfer status only exists if at least one operation of that kind was done for the specified filetype.

Yes, but it is off by default. set http-file-server [enabled] [http-enabled] [https-enabled] [http-port] [https-port] and show http-file-server (which also shows url-base) run in Operational and Candidate Configuration mode. enabled is the master switch to enable or disable file server access and defaults to true. http-enabled enables plain HTTP and defaults to false; https-enabled defaults to true. The default http-port is 8980 and the default https-port is 8981; both are user configurable numbers. url-base is the base URL used to redirect to the file transfer application, a string of 1 to 100 characters with the value /transfer.

Use the manifest commands in Operational or Candidate Configuration mode. show manifest-<manifest-file> [manifest-signature] [downloaded-on] [information] gives the manifest itself: manifest-signature is a hex-string up to 1024, downloaded-on is the download timestamp in YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ssZ format, and information is a string up to 256. show manifest-component-<manifest-file>/<equipment-type>/<name> [state] [version] [description] gives each package: state is installed, not-installed, installation-failed or unknown (default unknown), version is up to 64 characters and description up to 512. show manifest-firmware-<manifest-file>/<equipment-type>/<fw-name> [fw-version] gives the firmware carried per equipment-type.

No. The packaged-fw command shows the firmware version included in a software-load, and versions for the same firmware can be different per equipment-type. Use show packaged-fw-<location-id>/<swload-state>/<equipment-type>/<fw-name> [fw-version] or show packaged-fw-<swload-state>/<equipment-type>/<fw-name> [fw-version], in Operational or Candidate Configuration mode; show packaged-fw lists them all. location-id is <chassis-id>-<slot-id> (string 0-64). swload-state is active, inactive or installable. equipment-type is the card or other equipment type that will use the firmware (0-32 characters), fw-name is the firmware name (0-32) and fw-version the included version (0-32).

Yes. prepare-upgrade has two options: validate, which validates the software label or manifest, and apply, which applies it. Syntax: prepare-upgrade [-f] [-i] [-u] option=<value> manifest=<value> [db-action=<value>] [clear-type=<value>] script=<value> new-admin-user=<value> new-admin-password=<value>, in Operational mode. Flags: -h help, -i ignore validation failures, -u unattended (auto-activate software after prepare-upgrade apply), -f force without confirmation. Example: prepare-upgrade validate <label>, then prepare-upgrade apply <label>. db-action (unattended only) is empty-db, upgrade-db or rollback, default upgrade-db. clear-type is full (default), keep-networking or initialize-from-script, and is only valid for an unattended operation with db-action empty-db.

clear recover-mode clears the recover-mode flag. It clears the current recover-mode state of the NE, confirming the current configuration as is, re-enabling communication with the line cards and potentially reconfiguring the traffic settings. As such, it may be traffic impacting. The command has no parameters. Syntax: clear [-f] recover-mode, in Operational mode. The only flag is -f, which forces the command without the confirmation prompt: clear -f recover-mode.

Use show software-load-<swload-state> or show software-load-<location-id>/<swload-state>, in Operational or Candidate Configuration mode. swload-state is active (active software load), inactive (inactive software load) or installable (installable software load). Attributes are swload-version, swload-manifest and swload-prepared (true/false, both only relevant for the installable load), swload-status, swload-information, swload-activation-type, swload-vendor, swload-product, swload-label, swload-delta-label and swload-pkg-type. swload-activation-type applies only to state installable and is direct (no reboot type determined), warmstart (warm reboot required) or coldstart (cold reboot required). Examples: show software-load-active, show software-load-1-5/active.

Use show software-location-<location-id>, in Operational or Candidate Configuration mode. location-id is the location of the equipment, a string of up to 64 characters, expressed as <chassis-id>-<slot-id>. For example, show software-location-1-5 retrieves software location information from the card in chassis 1, slot 5. To narrow it to a particular load state on that slot, use show sw-management software-location-<shelf>-<slot> software-load-active (or software-load-inactive or software-load-installable), for example show sw-management software-location-1-4 software-load-active, which returns the software-load-1-4/active entry with its sw-component list, swload-version, swload-vendor, swload-product and swload-label.

Use show subtype-constraint-<card-type>/<subtype> [min-capacity] [max-capacity] [supported-applications] [unsupported-applications] [description], in Operational or Candidate Configuration mode. card-type and subtype each represent a group of related PONs for a card type to which the constraints apply, strings of 1 to 20 characters. min-capacity is the minimum capacity supported by the subtype in gbps and max-capacity the maximum in gbps, where -1 means there is no maximum capacity constraint. supported-applications lists the applications supported by the subtype and unsupported-applications those not supported; if either list is empty, that constraint is not applicable. description is a string of 1 to 255 characters.

Use show sw-component-<location-id>/<swload-state>/<name> [state] [version] [description], or show sw-component-<swload-state>/<name> when not scoping to a slot; Operational and Candidate Configuration mode. The state attribute is the package state: installed (software package installed), not-installed (not installed), installation-failed (install failed) or unknown (state unknown), with unknown as the default, so installation-failed is what you look for. location-id is <chassis-id>-<slot-id> and swload-state is active, inactive or installable. version is up to 64 characters and description up to 512. Examples: show sw-component, show sw-component-1-5/active/frcu31_ztp_pkg.

Use show sw-container-<container-name> [equipment] [state] [description] [cpu-usage] [memory-usage] [uptime], which lists the OS-level containers; Operational and Candidate Configuration mode. cpu-usage is the current CPU usage by the container as a percentage in the range 0 to 100, and in a multi-core system it indicates the overall usage relative to all cores. memory-usage is the current memory usage as a percentage, range 0 to 100. state is off (default state, the container is not launched yet), up (running) or exited. equipment is a reference to the card AID on which the container runs, and uptime is the time since the container started. Examples: show sw-container, show sw-container-frcu31-1-5_pyapi.

Yes. sw-control-rule adds service-specific custom rules that override the default action upon service failure. Syntax: add sw-control-rule-<service-name> fail-action <value>, set sw-control-rule-<service-name> [fail-action <value>], show sw-control-rule-<service-name> [fail-action], delete sw-control-rule-<service-name>; Operational and Candidate Configuration mode. service-name is the name of the service to be monitored, a string up to 64 characters. fail-action values are default-action (restart the service, then reboot the system if the service does not recover), ignore (no automatic action on service failure) and system-restart (warm restart the system or card software immediately on failure). Example: add sw-control-rule-xmm4-1-1_host_KeyManagement fail-action default-action.

Yes. show sw-management gives software locations, activity and downloads in one place, in Operational or Candidate Configuration mode. Syntax: show sw-management [downloads | software-location-<shelf>-<slot> [software-load-active | software-load-inactive | software-load-installable] | software-load-active | software-load-inactive]. show sw-management downloads lists the download history, for example the downloaded manifest files. show sw-management software-load-active lists the active load's sw-component and packaged-fw entries plus swload-version, swload-information, swload-vendor, swload-product, swload-label and swload-delta-label; software-load-inactive does the same for the inactive load. show sw-management software-location-1-4 software-load-active scopes it to one shelf and slot.

Use show sw-service-<sv-name> [equipment] [location] [state] [state-details] [cpu-usage] [memory-usage] [uptime] [last-start-time] [reboot-count], or show sw-services for all of them; Operational and Candidate Configuration mode. reboot-count is the number of times a service has restarted, a uint16. Pair it with last-start-time, the time of the last service start or boot, a date-time in YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ssZ format, and uptime, the time since the service turned up in days:hours:minutes. state is off (not being monitored), ok (ready and functional) or fail (failed to launch or unresponsive), with state-details giving a brief description. Example: show sw-service-frcu31-1-5_host_DpEncrMgr.

sw-subcomponent drills one level below sw-component: it keys on the subcomponent inside a package rather than the package itself. Syntax: show sw-subcomponent-<location-id>/<swload-state>/<sw-component-name>/<sw-subcomponent-name> [state] [version] [description], or show sw-subcomponent-<swload-state>/<sw-component-name>/<sw-subcomponent-name>; Operational and Candidate Configuration mode. sw-component-name and sw-subcomponent-name are strings of 1 to 256 characters. The reported attributes are the same set as sw-component: state (installed, not-installed, installation-failed, unknown, default unknown), version (0-64) and description (0-512). Example: show sw-subcomponent-1-5/active/frcu31_ztp_pkg/ztp.deb, versus show sw-component-1-5/active/frcu31_ztp_pkg.

Run swversion. It retrieves the active, inactive and installable versions of the software present on the network element, takes no parameters, and works in Operational and Candidate Configuration mode. The output lists software-load-active, software-load-inactive and software-load-installable at NE level with the version and label, and then the same three states per location, for example software-load-1-1/active, software-load-1-1/inactive and software-load-1-1/installable. A sample line reads: software-load-active R4.0.0 G40-R4.0.0-F-2021.06.03_08_22-sim-188. For more detail on any one entry use show software-load-<state> or show sw-management.

Use show third-party-fw-<fw-name> [file-status] [path] [version] [crc] [vendor] [part-number] [nsa-upgrade-version] [present-in-eqpt] [applicable-eqpt], in Operational or Candidate Configuration mode. file-status is the firmware file status with values valid, invalid or missing. crc is the cyclic redundancy check of the firmware image, used to validate the file when present, up to 64 characters. applicable-eqpt is the list of resources that this firmware can be applied to and present-in-eqpt the list of resources that contain this version, each with max-elements 80. path (up to 255), version, vendor and part-number (each up to 64) identify the image, and nsa-upgrade-version lists the versions from which the upgrade is non service affecting.

Set it with set transfer http-proxy <value> and read it back with show transfer [debug-log-optional-content] [http-proxy], in Operational or Candidate Configuration mode. http-proxy is the proxy server for internally-generated HTTP requests leaving the NE, which includes certificate revocation-related requests, that is CRL downloads and OCSP requests. Note that this proxy is not used for file transfers. The value is a string up to 1024 characters in the format [http://]<host>[:<port>], where http:// is optional, host may be the IPv4 address, IPv6 address or DNS name of the proxy server, and port is optional; if port is omitted the default is 1080. Example: set transfer http-proxy http://1.2.3.4:1080.

Use show transfer-status-<filetype>/<operation> [last-completion-status] [last-transfer] [last-duration] [transfer-type] [session-id] [session-user-name] [filename] [transfer-progress] [bytes-transferred] [total-bytes] [details], or plain show transfer-status for all entries. operation is upload or download. transfer-progress is the completion percentage, 0-100, default 0; bytes-transferred is the bytes transferred so far and total-bytes the total file size, both uint64 defaulting to 0, with total-bytes zero until known at transfer start. details gives the transfer phase: completed, Failed, idle, preparation or transfer, default idle. last-completion-status may be success, fail, in-progress or unknown, where unknown occurs if the system rebooted mid-transfer. transfer-type is sync or async.

Use show upgrade-status-<resource> [to-swload-version] [status] [start-time] [end-time] [step] [step-start-time] [details], in Operational or Candidate Configuration mode. resource may represent the entire ne, a chassis or a card; for ne and chassis the results are aggregated summaries of all cards in that scope, so start at ne and drill down to find the failing card. status values include idle, upgrade-in-progress, upgrade-complete, upgrade-partially-failed, upgrade-failed, validate-in-progress/failed/complete, apply-in-progress/failed/complete, activate-in-progress/failed/complete, cancel-in-progress/complete/failed and no-communication; default idle. step is the identifier of the current upgrade step and step-start-time when it began; start-time and end-time show na if the entity was idle or has not finished a phase since startup. details carries up to 255 characters of explanation.

Use upload [-a] [-s] filetype=debug-log with either destination=<URL> or file-server=<name> [path=<value>]; debug-log uploads logs for diagnostic troubleshooting and includes all other logs. debug-entity is mandatory for debug-log and restricts collection to a particular card or chassis; if absent all data is included. optional-content adds optional content to debug-logs. -a runs the upload asynchronously (check it with show transfer-status); in synchronous mode a textual progress bar is rendered live. -s skips TLS verification for HTTPS and ssh known host checking for SCP/SFTP. Certificates differ: for local-certificate, peer-certificate and trusted-certificate you must give certificate-name, except for trusted-certificate where omitting it exports all trusted certificates as a bundle. Only the public part is exported, private keys are not, and output files are in P7 pem format.

Use show ztp [ztp-mode] [ztp-state] [ztp-details] [ztp-completion-status], in Operational or Candidate Configuration mode. ztp-state is the current state of the ZTP service, with values ztp-init (the default), dhcp-in-progress, image-download-in-progress, image-install-in-progress, custom-script-execution-in-progress, multi-chassis-setup-in-progress, configuration-apply-in-progress, ztp-completed, ztp-state-unknown, ztp-disabled and wait-before-ztp-restart. ztp-details adds information on the current state, up to 256 characters. ztp-completion-status summarizes ZTP on the node as not-completed (default) or completed. ztp-mode is the user-set mode, disabled or enabled with enabled as the default, and is set via the change-ztp-mode RPC, which is allowed even when the NBI is locked.
